implemented_requirements.evidence: board.py defines BOARD_SIZE = 8 and creates an 8x8 grid in Board.__init__.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Two players alternate placing discs (black and white)
implemented_requirements.evidence: game.py sets self.current_player = BLACK and switches turns in Game._advance_turn using Board.get_opponent.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Flipping opponent discs that lie between the new disc and existing discs of the same colour
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.get_flippable_discs computes discs to flip; Board.make_move flips them.
Board.is_valid_move and Board.get_valid_moves return all legal positions; GUI draws hints using these.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Game ends when board is full or no valid moves remain
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.is_full and Board.has_valid_move are used in Game._advance_turn and Game.check_game_over to call _end_game.
Board.count_discs returns (black, white); GUI._draw_status renders the scores.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Pass handling when a player has no valid moves
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game._advance_turn sets self.message = "No valid move - pass!" and keeps the same current_player.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Graphical interface for playing the game
implemented_requirements.evidence: gui.py implements a pygame based GUI that draws the board, discs, hints, and processes mouse clicks.

judge.summary: The provided source files implement a complete Reversi/Othello game: an 8x8 board with correct move validation, disc flipping, turn management, pass handling, end‑game detection, scoring, and a pygame GUI that visualises the board and scores. The code is syntactically correct and, assuming pygame is installed, should run without modification. No major functional gaps or critical bugs were found.
